chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Zurbi narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to me from Abdillah ibn Marhum al-Azdi, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

One who fasts on the first day of Shaban, Paradise becomes obligatory for him. And one who fasts for two days, Allah looks at him every day and night in the dwelling of this world, and His gaze remains upon him in Paradise. And one who fasts for three days, Allah visits him upon His Throne from His Paradise every day.

key_terms.الْجَنَّهُ: Paradise, the abode of eternal bliss.
key_terms.دَارِ الدُّنْیَا: The dwelling of the world (this life).
key_terms.شَعْبَان: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.
key_terms.عَرْشِهِ: His Throne, symbolizing divine proximity and honor.

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for fasting on the first days of Shaban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the unique spiritual status of Shaban as a preparatory month for Ramadan, where specific days of fasting yield escalating divine honors. The progression from guaranteed Paradise to the intimate honor of Allah’s visitation on His Throne underscores the concept of *tawassul* through voluntary acts, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and merit-based nature of worship in the months preceding the obligatory fast.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4.  The narrator says that he heard Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) say, “One who fasts on first of Shaban then surely, Paradise would be made obligatory for him. If he observes two fasts, the  Almighty  Allah would look  at him  with mercy  in this world  every  day  and  night.  He  would  also  shower  His mercy  on  him  in  Paradise.  One  who  fasts  for  three  days would  get  to  visit  Allah  daily  on  the  Divine  throne  in Paradise.”
